clue.text: Economical vehicle switches fuel

indicators.note: to switch things round is to swap their positions, so the letters of the next word change places

blocks.note: a car is an everyday vehicle
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An advert for a thrifty car that runs on a different kind of fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone careful with money is thrifty, so the word is a synonym for sparing in spending.

clue.text: Not needed with an automatic grip

blocks.note: first meaning: the pedal a manual car has and an automatic gearbox does without
second meaning: a tight hold or grasp

explanation.surface: A driving tip that an automatic car spares you the effort of holding on.
explanation.definitionFit: The pedal disengaging the gears is absent in automatics, and as a noun the word also means a firm grasp.

clue.text: Respectable Democrat replaced by Republican not long ago

definitions.note: adverbial phrase; the answer is the adjective, 'of not long ago'

indicators.note: one thing replaced by another means the first letter is swapped out for the second

blocks.note: respectable and decent are synonyms
D is the abbreviation for Democrat, the letter removed
R is the abbreviation for Republican, the letter put in

explanation.surface: A respectable Democrat lost a seat to a Republican in a recent election.
explanation.walkthrough: DECENT with its D swapped for R gives RECENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recent happened or appeared lately, at a time close to the present.

clue.text: Threatening reshuffle for a Lib-Dem

indicators.note: a reshuffle rearranges a set of people or cards into a new order, as these letters are

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A political cabinet reshuffle that menaces a Liberal Democrat's position.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lib-Dem is a member of Britain's Liberal Democrat party; 'reshuffle' is a political word here doing anagram work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something formidable inspires fear or dread through its power, so it is menacing.

clue.text: The French greeting when on holiday

blocks.note: le is a French word for 'the'
ave is the Latin greeting 'hail'

explanation.surface: How the French say hello when they are away on vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'on leave' is to be on holiday, which is why the clue phrases it 'when on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave is time off granted from work or service, the military and British term for a vacation.

clue.text: Drop in last month's score

blocks.note: December is the last month of the year; DEC is its abbreviation
to score is to mark with a line

explanation.surface: Reporting a fall in a team's or pupil's score compared with last month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' suggests twenty or a result; here it is the verb sense of marking a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A decline is a fall or decrease, the same as a drop in level.

clue.text: Attractive guy, not fully dressed, is found in the kitchen

indicators.note: not fully means the word is cut short, losing its end

blocks.note: a dish is slang for a good-looking person
clothed means dressed

explanation.surface: A half-dressed hunk is discovered in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: CLOTHED loses its last two letters. The definition is descriptive rather than a synonym: a dishcloth is a thing found in a kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishcloth is a cloth for washing dishes, an item kept by the kitchen sink.

clue.text: Affected about a Westminster politician

blocks.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
taken as written
a Member of Parliament sits at Westminster

explanation.surface: Describing a Westminster MP as rather pretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container signal but here simply gives C, for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp behaviour is exaggerated and theatrical, so it is affected or mannered.

clue.text: I will deal with abuse

blocks.note: I'll is the contraction of I will
to treat a matter is to deal with it

explanation.surface: Someone promising to handle a case of abuse personally.
explanation.definitionFit: To ill-treat someone is to mistreat or harm them, which is what abusing means.

clue.text: In the end Poles are trapped

indicators.note: in places the following words inside the next one

blocks.note: S and N are the south and north poles
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Polish people finally caught in some trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland but means the compass points north and south.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensnared means caught as in a snare, so it is a synonym for trapped.

clue.text: Sore from cruel treatment

indicators.note: treatment here means rough handling, so the word is processed into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone left sore after being treated cruelly.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulcer is an open sore on the skin or a membrane, so it names a sore.

clue.text: Collects a Nazi unit badge, trimmed with silver originally

indicators.note: something trimmed has its end cut off
originally points to the start of a word, its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the SS was a Nazi paramilitary organisation
an emblem is a badge or symbol
the first letter of silver

explanation.surface: A collector of militaria acquiring an SS insignia edged in silver.
explanation.walkthrough: EMBLEM loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble things is to gather them together, the same as collecting them.

clue.text: Trust prisoner to dispose of loot without papers

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: con is short for convict
to fence stolen goods is to sell them on
identity papers, ID

explanation.surface: Trusting a convict to get rid of stolen goods when he has no documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but in crosswords it can mean outside. A fence is a receiver of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Confidence is firm belief or faith in someone, a synonym of trust.

clue.text: District is more open, we are told

indicators.note: what we are told is heard, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: airier means more open and breezy

explanation.surface: Claiming one neighbourhood is more spacious than another.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent airier and area sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or zone, which a district is.

clue.text: Information put out in favour of godless American lawyer

blocks.note: pro means for, in favour of
a pagan does not follow a mainstream religion
a DA is a District Attorney in the US

explanation.surface: A press release backing an atheist US attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is biased information spread to promote a cause, material deliberately disseminated.

clue.text: Suited to take over

blocks.note: first meaning, an adjective: fitting or proper
second meaning, a verb: to seize for one's own use

explanation.surface: Someone fit to assume control of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'suited to' as one phrase; 'to' is really just a link between the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means fitting; as a verb, said differently, it means to seize something without permission.

clue.text: Constant peril, involving an enemy navy initially being at sea

indicators.note: initially points to the first letters of the words before it
being at sea means confused and disoriented, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first letters of enemy and navy

explanation.surface: Sailors face a never-ending danger from a hostile fleet out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Perennial means lasting or recurring year after year, so it is a synonym of constant.

clue.text: Spies act out a Walter Mitty character?

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Spies acting out a daydreamer's fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Mitty is the daydreaming hero of a James Thurber story who imagines himself in heroic roles, such as a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Walter Mitty retreats into fantasy to avoid dull reality, which is exactly what an escapist does.

clue.text: Stick up for the man I love keeping married name

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside

blocks.note: a chap is a man
M is the abbreviation for married
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Defending a beloved partner who kept her married name.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAP holds M, then I, O and N follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause or person is to support and defend them publicly.

clue.text: Polish crash disrupted financial support for students

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A crash in Poland upsets funding for students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' could be the verb, but its capital letter leads the surface to the nationality; either way it is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholarship is a grant of money awarded to pay for a student's education.

clue.text: Make off with sailor's pipe

blocks.note: an AB is an able seaman
a duct is a pipe or channel

explanation.surface: Someone stealing a seaman's tobacco pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct is to carry off a person by force, i.e. to make off with them.

clue.text: Give money back to daughter after funeral is endlessly re-arranged

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its ending
re-arranged means put in a different order
after means one piece is placed following the other

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Reimbursing a daughter after her parent's funeral plans change.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'endlessly' removes two letters, AL, rather than the usual one, leaving FUNER to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A refund is a repayment, and to refund is to return money to the payer.

clue.text: A regularly grumpy host

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every other letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered person hosting a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like a party-giver but means a large crowd or army.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is, in an older sense, a great multitude or army, as in the heavenly host.

clue.text: Ruled out backing Big Issue initially in popular women's magazine

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before
backing means going backwards, so the letters run in reverse
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
Elle is a fashion magazine for women
taken as written
the first letter of Issue

explanation.surface: A women's magazine refusing to support the Big Issue.
explanation.walkthrough: The Big Issue is a British magazine sold by homeless people; here only its first word and the initial of the second are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ineligible does not meet the conditions, so they are disqualified or excluded.

clue.text: Ship some of the petrol in error

indicators.note: some of means only part of the following words is used, a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the next two

explanation.surface: Putting the wrong petrol in a vessel's tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner is a large passenger ship sailing a regular route.

clue.text: Fine with a strong breeze

blocks.note: f is forte, the musical direction for loud or strong
air is a light breeze

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: fine, with a strong wind.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a forecast, so 'strong breeze' looks like one item; it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair weather is fine and dry, so fair and fine are synonyms in forecasts.

clue.text: I'm working to protect international film-maker from cheap copy

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround and shield it

blocks.note: taken as written
a machine that is on is working
I is the abbreviation for international
Jacques Tati was a French film director

explanation.surface: A film-maker's agent defending him against cheap knock-offs.
explanation.walkthrough: IM and ON together surround I and TATI.
explanation.definitionFit: An imitation is a copy made to resemble the genuine article, often an inferior fake.

clue.text: Run madly to secure gold for Pacific island

indicators.note: madly means wildly and without order, so the letters are jumbled
to secure something is to hold it fast inside

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Racing frantically to grab treasure for a South Seas island.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a small island nation in the Pacific Ocean, in Micronesia.

clue.text: Tungsten drill bit which is used to support a climber

indicators.note: a bit is a part, so only a portion of the words is used

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A hard metal drill bit for fixing anchors that hold a rock climber.
explanation.walkthrough: The climber is a climbing plant, not a mountaineer; 'Tungsten' tempts W, its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is a slender coiling shoot that a climbing plant uses to cling to supports.

clue.text: Gave feedback about performance by journalist

blocks.note: re means about, concerning
an act is a performance
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A journalist's review responding to a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond to something, which is what giving feedback is.
